name: ember lamp
desc: A small brass lamp with a pinhole of living ember at its heart. It was in your hand when you woke.

extras.text: The ember is dim and sulky. You should rest soon.
The ember has dimmed a little, but still holds.
The ember burns bright and steady.

useAlone.text: You turn the lamp's little wheel. The ember flares politely, then settles. It burns only when you need it to, in dark places, and rests when you do.

name: pair of spectacles
desc: Thick round lenses in a wire frame, bent at one temple. Wick's, surely: nobody else would need lenses this thick.

name: flask of lamp oil
desc: A stoppered flask of clear gold oil that smells of warm summer evenings.

name: coil of rope
desc: A long coil of salt-stiff rope. Strong enough to hold your weight, if properly attached to something.

name: stone apple
desc: An apple carved out of grey granite, warm from the sun. Pell would probably like it.
takeText: It is heavier than it looks, but not unpleasant.

name: iron hook
desc: A heavy, three-pronged iron hook with an eyelet at one end. It would grip nearly anything, if it had a line.

name: grappling hook
desc: An iron hook knotted firmly to a long rope. A proper grapple, ready to catch hold of a pillar across a gulf.

name: shard of mirror
desc: A flat, bright shard of silvered glass. It throws a dancing spot of light when you tilt it.

name: valve wheel
desc: A heavy iron wheel with a square hole at its centre, rusty but sound. It looks as if it would fit a valve stem.

name: clump of glowmoss
desc: A soft handful of glowing moss. It smells of rain and could brighten a flagging lamp.

useAlone.text: You rub the moss against the ember. The lamp drinks in its glow, and burns brighter than before.

name: pair of tongs
desc: Long iron tongs with wooden grips, built for holding things too hot or too holy to touch.

name: salt-stiff ledger
desc: A thick book swollen with salt, its cover stamped with a bell.
readText: You pry the pages open. Most are lost, but one entry is clear: 'THE HUSH IS CALLED BY THREE BELLS, RUNG IN THE ORDER THE HEART KEEPS. IT BEGINS AT THE HEART, THEN SINKS TO THE ROOT, THEN CLIMBS TO THE SKY. SING IT WRONG AND IT UNSINGS ITSELF.'

name: Lantern of Tide
desc: A lantern of green glass and blue fire, light that moves like water. It is cool in your hand and smells of deep places.
takeText: As you lift it, a long breath moves through the cathedral, and the water remembers where the sea is.

name: Lantern of Ember
desc: A lantern of black iron with a heart of living ember, steadily warm against your tongs.
takeBlocked: You reach out, and the heat of the Lantern of Ember bites your fingers. You snatch your hand back. It would take something long and iron to lift this.
takeText: Held in the tongs, the lantern burns sweetly, a coal that will not go out.

name: Lantern of Hush
desc: A lantern of frosted glass holding a light so gentle it seems to be listening to you.
takeText: The moment you lift it, the whole world seems to draw a quiet, grateful breath.

name: piece of sea glass
desc: A frosted lozenge of green glass, rounded by years of sea. It glows faintly in the dark.

name: grey feather
desc: A long grey heron feather, soft as a held breath.

name: bent spoon
desc: A tarnished silver spoon, bent at an angle that suggests a great deal of effort or a great deal of boredom.

name: lucky coin
desc: A worn copper coin with a tiny lamp stamped on one side and a tiny moon on the other. It feels warm, like it's been loved.

name: whispering shell
desc: A spiral shell. Held to the ear, it whispers, very quietly: 'you were brave.'
readText: You hold the shell to your ear. 'It was only the dark,' it whispers.

name: pocket moon
desc: A marble of pale light the size of a plum. A lamp-maker's prized work, perhaps never sold because it was too good.

useAlone.text: You cup the little moon in your hands and breathe on it. Warm light floods into your lamp, refilling it to the brim.

name: silver drop
desc: A drop of liquid silver that does not roll, does not sink, and does not stop being a little bit of the moon.

useAlone.text: You tip the silver drop into your lamp. The ember brightens to a clear, cold white, and your lamp is filled to the brim.

name: unfinished map
desc: A map of the Hollowmere with many rooms still blank, and a note: 'Perhaps you will fill them in.'
